summary: 1. Prioritize personal human biology and active bodily phenomena over passive external physics or general engineering objects. 2. Hook the viewer in sentence one using second-person active confrontation ('Your eyes are leaking right now') rather than hypothetical scenarios or rhetorical setup questions. 3. Frame titles and hooks around a clear myth-bust or paradoxical subversion rather than explaining a standard factual process. 4. Eliminate all narrative warm-up; state the immediate visceral contradiction within the first 7 words. 5. Keep script duration tight, aiming for 18-25 seconds of punchy explanation to maintain retention.
winning_hooks: Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.
This shark is older than the United States.
avoid: Opening hooks with passive rhetorical questions like 'Ever noticed those tiny black dots...?' (stayed_pct: 36.9%).
Hypothetical storytelling setups like 'Your car swerves off the highway...' (stayed_pct: 30.4%).
Topics focused on ambient outdoor/material physics rather than human-centric biological mechanisms (e.g., pond ice at 23.7%, guardrails at 30.4%).
Reciting well-known trivia as the main hook without a surprising counter-twist (e.g., 'Honey never spoils' at 38.6%).
next_experiment: A/B test a biological myth topic strictly under 25 seconds using the formula: '[Body reaction] isn't caused by [popular belief], it's actually [surprising biological mechanism]' (e.g., 'Your stomach growling isn't caused by hunger...') to target a stayed_pct above 60%.
